title: Does the Gender Composition of Scientific Committees Matter?
notes: OK (no benefit of more women evaluators). Abstract (p.1207): 100,000 applications to associate/full professorships in Italy and Spain, 8,000 randomly selected evaluators: 'A larger number of women in evaluation committees does not increase either the quantity or the quality of female candidates who qualify'; male evaluators become less favorable to female candidates once a female evaluator joins. Fig. 1: effects by discipline mostly n.s.
